title: The mass and mean length of critical bridges in a fixed-width corridor
exact_target: For critical honeycomb bridge weights spanning pure cuts at separation R, does there exist $C_0$ such that for every fixed corridor aspect $C\geq C_0$, the confined and unconfined total masses are comparable to $R^{-1/4}$, their first length masses are $R^(13/12+o(1))$, and both normalized mean lengths are $R^(4/3+o(1))$?
definition_tex:
\subsection{Definitions and mathematical statement}
\paragraph{Statement recorded in the supplied source.}
For critical honeycomb bridge weights spanning pure cuts at separation R, does there exist $C_0$ such that for every fixed corridor aspect $C\geq C_0$, the confined and unconfined total masses are comparable to $R^{-1/4}$, their first length masses are $R^(13/12+o(1))$, and both normalized mean lengths are $R^(4/3+o(1))$?

\subsection{Short English statement}
For critical honeycomb bridge weights spanning pure cuts at separation R, does there exist $C_0$ such that for every fixed corridor aspect $C\geq C_0$, the confined and unconfined total masses are comparable to $R^{-1/4}$, their first length masses are $R^(13/12+o(1))$, and both normalized mean lengths are $R^(4/3+o(1))$?
